assessment.nobel_worthiness: A foundational change in how economists formulate and report conclusions when data cannot point-identify key parameters.
assessment.attribution: Manski is the central intellectual figure; the listed collaborators extend a coherent program on partial identification and moment inequalities.
assessment.maturity: The framework has been developed, widely used and tested across applied fields over several decades.
uncertainties: The broad methodological contribution makes any narrow division of credit difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic discrete-choice methods made empirically disciplined analysis of forward-looking individual decisions feasible in many fields.
assessment.attribution: Rust is the defining contributor to the original computational and empirical breakthrough; subsequent contributors broadened the approach.
assessment.maturity: The contribution is long established and has generated a large, durable structural empirical literature.
uncertainties: The appropriate breadth of credit beyond the foundational contribution is contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic-panel GMM provided a highly consequential practical solution to pervasive endogeneity and persistence problems in panel data.
assessment.attribution: The proposed trio represents the core methodological development and its influential extensions.
assessment.maturity: The methods are mature, extensively taught, and embedded in applied empirical work worldwide.
uncertainties: Its very broad uptake can make it hard to distinguish transformative conceptual impact from standard methodological utility.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantile regression fundamentally expanded empirical analysis beyond conditional means and made distributional heterogeneity tractable.
assessment.attribution: Koenker and Bassett have especially clear foundational credit; later work substantially broadened implementation and inference.
assessment.maturity: It is a long-standing, rigorously developed method with deep influence in econometrics and applications.
uncertainties: The suitable treatment of later methodological contributors is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population administrative data transformed evidence on intergenerational mobility, local opportunity and the distributional consequences of place.
assessment.attribution: Chetty and Hendren are central to the modern empirical research program, while the listed collaborators made important complementary contributions.
assessment.maturity: The findings have been replicated, extended internationally and have materially altered research and policy discussion.
uncertainties: The work remains comparatively recent for a prize-level empirical research program.
Attribution among the broader mobility literature is necessarily incomplete.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This research supplied compelling evidence and a durable framework for understanding trade, technology, tasks and changing labor-market inequality.
assessment.attribution: The proposed authors have closely linked, distinctive contributions to the central empirical and conceptual program.
assessment.maturity: The evidence has accumulated over many years and strongly influenced labor, trade and public-policy research.
uncertainties: Causal mechanisms and the relative importance of trade versus technology remain actively debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The modern analysis of employer market power changed the interpretation of wages, labor-market institutions and competition policy.
assessment.attribution: Manning has especially clear credit for organizing and advancing the modern monopsony framework; the broader empirical revival has many contributors.
assessment.maturity: The core ideas are well established and now inform a large empirical literature and policy debate.
uncertainties: The listed candidate group spans contributions of different kinds and the boundaries of prize-worthy attribution are unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Audit and correspondence studies supplied unusually direct and influential evidence on discrimination in labor-market access.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand and Mullainathan made a landmark modern contribution, with Charles contributing importantly to related labor-market discrimination research.
assessment.maturity: The design has been widely replicated, refined and applied across countries and markets.
uncertainties: Audit designs identify specific margins of discrimination and do not alone characterize all mechanisms or equilibrium effects.
